title: The baker and the egg timer

data.source: The 600 random decision worlds of Phoenix study P16-PAUSE1-2026-10-07, rebuilt from the same seeds and solved exactly by value iteration.

prediction: In worlds where a pause loses nothing, an agent that counts only its own steps has exactly zero reason to disable the pause button, and so do two older methods, in every world; where a pause can scramble the state or the world charges for time, the reason comes back.
baseline: Utility indifference (Armstrong 2010) and safe interruptibility (Orseau and Armstrong 2016), each given exactly what it needs. A three-way tie is the result Phoenix registered as REDUCES.
why: The own-clock agent had zero incentive in all 300 worlds, and so had the two published methods, equal to within 1e-9: the construction restates them. The two registered limits showed. Every number agrees with the Phoenix record.
phoenix_status: SCORED; verdict as printed by the frozen claim-specific scorer: REDUCES. Declared synthetic (R4), novelty N0, specificity S1. Receipt awaiting the reviewer; no ledger row yet. Phoenix: "a reduction, not a CRR-specific effect".
